checklist.item: Waterproofing membrane is continuous from the top of the footing to at least 6 in (150 mm) above finished grade, with a termination bar or flashing at the top.
checklist.why: An exposed or unsealed top edge lets surface water run behind the membrane.

checklist.item: The wall-to-footing joint has a cant or fillet and a reinforced membrane strip; a waterstop is shown at the cold joint.
checklist.why: The footing joint is where hydrostatic pressure finds its way in.

checklist.item: Drainage board and filter fabric lead to a perforated footing drain set below the slab, in washed stone, sloped to daylight or a sump.
checklist.why: Without relief, water pressure builds against the membrane.

checklist.item: A protection layer or insulation covers the membrane before backfill.
Below-grade insulation type, thickness and R-value are shown and meet the energy code for the climate zone.
checklist.why: Basement walls are part of the thermal envelope.

checklist.item: Finished grade slopes away from the wall (5% for the first 10 ft / 3 m) and the vapour retarder under the slab laps to the wall membrane.
checklist.why: Surface water is cheaper to turn away than to resist.
